scope: Source-grounded scientific acceptance review of Temporal replacement candidates 037 and 047. All old frozen run artifacts were read only.

method.primary_evidence: Each frozen source_packet.txt was compared byte-for-byte with its paired source.tex without hashing, and scientific claims were checked against exact inclusive source.tex line anchors.
method.identity_cross_check: The versioned arXiv records and DOI metadata were cross-checked against the official arXiv API and official Crossref DOI metadata. The academic-search MCP was unavailable, so these T1 official-source fallbacks were used.
method.highest_priority_gate: A Player control must be a numeric quantity actually manipulated or set in the reported study; a measured value, fitted quantity, uncertainty, theoretical parameter, or discrete sample label is not a control merely because it is numeric or enumerable.
method.continuous_domain_rule: A continuous interval was accepted only where the paper documents active variation or a sweep and a fitted relation over multiple settings. Interval endpoints were chosen conservatively from source-reported experimental bounds or explicitly reported settings, not invented to satisfy compilation.

reviews.frozen_rejection_reason: the source-supported Cartesian domain has no held-out condition after allocating the minimum diagnostic observations required for Identification
reviews.frozen_artifact_policy: Construct a new reviewed artifact from revised_science_card; do not alter the old frozen production run.

source_identity.title: Observation of Sine-Gordon-like Solitons in a Spinor Bose-Einstein Condensate

actual_manipulation_control_gate.rationale: The effective quadratic Zeeman shift q is actively tuned by off-resonant microwave dressing. The authors reliably vary q, repeat the time-evolution measurement for each q, and fit the resulting velocity. q_over_h is therefore an actual numeric intervention and is distinct from the measured soliton velocity and the fitted slope alpha.

line_ranges.evidence: The abstract states that soliton velocity can be tuned by the effective quadratic Zeeman shift.
The experiment tunes q by off-resonant microwave dressing, reliably varies it, records the observable for each q, extracts v, and fits v(q).
The apparatus description confirms that microwave dressing effectively tunes q into the relevant experimental regime.

continuous_interval_assessment.rationale: The source does not describe two isolated q settings: it reports reliable active variation, a measurement for each q, and a linear fit over the resulting multi-setting data. The post-offset non-moving setting defines q_over_h = 0, and q_over_h = 0.53 Hz is explicitly shown as an experimental setting. The closed interval from 0 to 0.53 Hz is a conservative interpolation within the reported fit evidence and does not claim the paper's full possible tuning range.

line_ranges.evidence: Figure 3 and the surrounding text document the multi-q linear relation, the explicit 0.53 Hz setting, and the subtracted zero-velocity origin.

source_evidence.supports: The system is a quasi-one-dimensional spin-1 rubidium-87 BEC with approximately flat atomic density, and q is defined as the quadratic Zeeman energy shift.

The isolated soliton is phase-imprinted; v is the soliton velocity; F_perp time evolution and position fits yield v for each tuned q; the experimental central fit is v(q)=alpha q/h with alpha=(40 plus or minus 3) um/(s*Hz).

Theory gives v/ell = plus or minus q/hbar; soliton width is density-dependent, and the experimental slope is consistent in scale but should not be transferred without holding the experimental setting fixed.
Different atomic densities require different microwave dressing and have separate linear velocity fits and density-dependent q offsets.
The simulation reports a different fitted slope, so the revised card explicitly uses the experimental central slope rather than the simulation value.

parameter_provenance.uncertainty_treatment: The plus-or-minus 3 value is fit uncertainty provenance, not per-query Oracle noise.

boundary_findings: The relation is limited to the isolated phase-imprinted sine-Gordon-like soliton in the quasi-one-dimensional spin-1 rubidium-87 BEC studied here.
q_over_h uses the experimentally subtracted offset for which the tuned non-moving soliton is q_over_h = 0.
The deterministic law uses the experimental central fit alpha = 40 um/(s*Hz), not the separate simulation slope.
Atomic density and the associated soliton-width setting must remain fixed; density-dependent offsets and separate unrescaled slopes prevent transfer across densities.
The accepted query interval is only 0 to 0.53 Hz and makes no claim about the full microwave-dressing range, negative q, collision experiments, or other soliton classes.

minimum_revision: Change the control domain from two numeric_values to the source-supported conservative continuous_interval [0.0, 0.53] Hz.
Retain alpha = 40 um/(s*Hz) as the deterministic experimental central fit and record the reported plus-or-minus 3 fit uncertainty only as provenance.
Add explicit offset, system, density, width, experimental-versus-simulation, and interval boundaries to applicability.

controls.definition: Post-offset effective quadratic Zeeman shift divided by Planck's constant, actively tuned with off-resonant microwave dressing for the multi-setting soliton-velocity measurement.
controls.name: q_over_h

applicability.statement: Experimental central-value fit for an isolated phase-imprinted sine-Gordon-like soliton in the quasi-one-dimensional spin-1 rubidium-87 condensate; q is actively varied by microwave dressing and v is obtained from position-versus-time fits.

q_over_h uses the experimentally subtracted offset for which the tuned non-moving soliton is q_over_h = 0; the conservative continuous query interval 0 to 0.53 Hz lies between that fit origin and the explicitly shown post-shift q_over_h = 0.53 Hz data within the reported multi-q linear fit.
The deterministic relation uses the fitted central slope alpha = 40 um/(s*Hz); the source reports fit uncertainty plus or minus 3 um/(s*Hz), which is provenance rather than per-query Oracle noise.

Atomic density and soliton width remain fixed at the main fit setting; the fitted slope and offset must not be transferred across densities because the source reports density-dependent offsets and noncoincident unrescaled slopes.

readouts.definition: Velocity of the isolated phase-imprinted soliton, extracted from a linear fit to its measured position over time for each tuned quadratic Zeeman shift.
readouts.name: v

source.citation: Yannick Deller, Observation of Sine-Gordon-like Solitons in a Spinor Bose-Einstein Condensate, Physical Review Letters (2026), DOI:10.1103/bpl2-y7ls

source_identity.title: Third-Order Nonlinear Transport in a Percolative Two-Dimensional Superconductor

actual_manipulation_control_gate.rationale: T is the sample temperature actively swept in cryogenic temperature-dependent resistance measurements. The paper reports measurements at different temperatures and says the experimental regimes are controlled by temperature. T is distinct from the fitted transition parameter Tc and the fitted critical-field readout Bc_perp, so it satisfies the actual-manipulation contract.

line_ranges.evidence: The paper reports the temperature-dependent resistance curve, defines Tc from that curve, and states the 250 mK cryostat base temperature.
The experiment explicitly measures transport curves at different temperatures.
The paper explicitly states that experimental transitions between regimes are controlled by temperature and excitation current.
Temperature-dependent resistance is measured under varied perpendicular fields to trace and fit the superconducting transition line.

continuous_interval_assessment.rationale: The source reports continuous temperature-dependent R-T curves and a continuous two-dimensional Ginzburg-Landau fit to the transition line, not two isolated temperature labels. The 0.25 K lower bound is the reported cryostat base temperature, and 1.4 K is the reported zero-field subcritical transition temperature. This conservative interval avoids extrapolating the fitted critical line below the measured base temperature.

line_ranges.evidence: The source reports the temperature-dependent resistance curve, full R-T data, Tc approximately 1.4 K, and a 250 mK base temperature.
Temperature-dependent resistance under varied fields yields a continuous fitted critical line described by the 2D GL relation.

source_evidence.supports: Device A is the main-text trilayer 1T-prime MoTe2 device; Tc approximately 1.4 K is defined at 50 percent of normal-state resistance; measurements use a pumped helium-3 cryostat with a 250 mK base temperature.

Temperature is an experimental control; temperature-dependent resistance under varied perpendicular fields is measured at 50 nA; the critical line follows Bc_perp = phi0/(2*pi*xi_GL^2)*(1-T/Tc), with an extrapolated critical field of approximately 0.9 T and xi_GL approximately 19.4 nm.

parameter_provenance.Bc_perp_0_interpretation: Approximate fitted zero-temperature field intercept, not an exact raw measurement.
parameter_provenance.Tc_interpretation: Approximate zero-field subcritical transition temperature defined at 50 percent of normal-state resistance.

boundary_findings: The relation is the approximate two-dimensional Ginzburg-Landau central fit for device A, a trilayer 1T-prime MoTe2 percolative superconductor.
Tc is operationally defined at 50 percent of the normal-state resistance; alternative transition criteria are outside scope.
The phase boundary is extracted from temperature-dependent resistance under varied perpendicular magnetic fields using a 50 nA excitation current.
Bc_perp_0 = 0.9 T is a fitted extrapolated zero-temperature intercept; the accepted Oracle never queries below the measured 0.25 K base temperature.
The relation must not be generalized to device B, other thicknesses or materials, parallel field, nonlinear-transport amplitude alpha-star, or temperatures outside 0.25 to 1.4 K.

minimum_revision: Change the T domain from two numeric_values to the source-supported conservative continuous_interval [0.25, 1.4] K.
Keep T as the actively swept control and distinguish it explicitly from the fitted Tc parameter and fitted Bc_perp readout.

Represent the source's approximate central fit as Bc_perp_0 = 0.9 T and Tc = 1.4 K, and add device, transition-definition, excitation-current, intercept, orientation, and no-below-base-temperature boundaries.

controls.definition: Sample temperature actively varied in the cryogenic temperature-dependent resistance measurements used to trace the perpendicular-field superconducting transition.
controls.name: T

applicability.statement: Approximate two-dimensional Ginzburg-Landau central fit for device A, a trilayer 1T-prime MoTe2 percolative superconductor; its zero-field subcritical transition temperature Tc is defined at 50 percent of the normal-state resistance and reported as approximately 1.4 K.

The critical line is extracted from temperature-dependent resistance under varied applied perpendicular magnetic fields using a 50 nA excitation current; Bc_perp_0 = approximately 0.9 T is the fitted zero-temperature field intercept and not an exact point measurement.

The conservative continuous query interval 0.25 to 1.4 K is bounded by the reported 250 mK cryostat base temperature and the reported zero-field Tc; it does not query the fitted relation below the measured base temperature.

readouts.definition: Perpendicular critical magnetic field on the superconducting phase boundary of device A, obtained from the fitted temperature-dependent transition line rather than a raw field reading at one temperature.
readouts.name: Bc_perp

source.citation: Wenjun Liu, Third-Order Nonlinear Transport in a Percolative Two-Dimensional Superconductor, Physical Review Letters (2026), DOI:10.1103/jcrm-953w
